## Design

### 2026-10-08 – Wednesday October 7: Schematics and footprint attempt

**2h**

Wednesday October 7: Schematics and footprint attempt

I created a new project and started following the Starbie guide on GitHub. I needed to download the symbol and footprint libraries first, but I accidentally put them in the same folder, so I had to redo it separately. I  started following the schematics in the guide. I didn't know how the net worked or what to do, so I watched a few YouTube videos to understand what they are.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/9fc9304c40ffe3862b2f291d0bd2d8543beefc184b1df8d433c870eab9d9600f.png)

The rest of the schematics were pretty straightforward, and I was able to finish them soon.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/ca06cb155108d24d7d0119ef5b11ce78ae2490ef6d4d6ee072bcb4899099abb2.png)

I started working on the footprints and added the .pretty folder library from the guide, but for some reason, it didn't work for a few tries. I tried to find how to do it online, but I still wasn't able to. I decided to just stop for the day and try later.

### 2026-10-09 – Thursday, October 8: footprints and edge cuts

**3h**

Thursday, October 8: footprints and edge cuts

I tried adding the guide's footprint libraries again and watched a few YouTube videos:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/9e8923d83ffe0cf2a4c70a0ce1ed8e19a749a70bbae1905c583ad631dc9ea1b2.png)

 I was doing the same thing as them, though, so I couldn't see where I was messing up. I tried it a few more times, and it miraculously worked the 3rd time.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/77f35139155a82d0eb3ac24f632be8fd22dc8ae8b1cb25ba6d6dfadaab889397.png)

After the footprints were done, I started editing the PCB and wanted to try making my own edge cut, as shown in the guide. I wanted to try a rounded hexagon shape for the edge cuts. I sadly wasn't able to do it well.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/fa0a099cd6412f88af69490a54f1fe4a40917cfc793e2162906c8d5e2bc1252b.png)

I wasn't able to figure out how to make defined shapes (apart from specifying x and y values), so I tried watching YouTube videos.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/94925367f1002398075eafcf9d8385ea25bbb3136647c59c29061cc539226bda.png)

I tried to find some information anywhere, but it looks like there was nothing I could do except use coordinates. I decided to leave and do it tomorrow.

### 2026-10-10 – Friday October 9:

**2h**

Friday October 9:

After spending so much time yesterday to find how to make defined shapes in edge cuts, I decided it would be better to just write coordinates. I made the hexagon shape pretty soon.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/332f41db53f020dd3334d34f0a03281051f548688bcd7955327b9e902da66568.png)

I spent a lot of time moving the components around to get an efficient layout. It took me a while, but I was able to get a decent one.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/b6ba912da723788eff416307027b873deadb8b06339170faff5ae5b05a6de56d.png)

I then installed the Arduino IDE, but for some reason, I couldn't get the ESP32 board. I tried many times, but it was just "processing" forever. I decided to try again tomorrow.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/e7f00a6ff64fca0ad66ebce387e0bebfbc196ba7f58a022eeff410f80cdc9fce.png)

### 2026-10-10 – I tried the Arduino IDE app again, but it still wasn't working. This time, it was sitting blank, and I couldn't click anything or close the app.

**3h**

I tried the Arduino IDE app again, but it still wasn't working. This time, it was sitting blank, and I couldn't click anything or close the app.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 083929](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/8d55ff29c2e0cd37c22f37cae90167be54c5a2ec48758dac2f347d36dbac3fca.png)

Finally, I used the Task Manager to close the app and open a new window, and it worked. After that, the rest of the firmware was simple, and I spent some time figuring out what I should draw for my pet. I decided to just make a smiley face, though.

![bitmap_good_pet_2.0](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/da4e8abf881614d756d5f6fa4e9edd378d6fbeae8929ee6d2e72c98da07519b4.png)

Then, I was about to finish and put everything on GitHub when I realized my PCB was wrong. I spent some time checking it and rewiring everything, but something was still wrong, and I couldn't figure out what. I undid everything and tried again, but it was still wrong. I decided to check the schematic to see if there were any problems, and then saw that I had labeled the 01x04 pin incorrectly.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/e7f618da43b316a7cdee3608cd94d679e9b575c9a0f18b184003f88c2fe02ad5.png)

I then fixed it and started working on the PCB for the 3rd time. Luckily, everything worked smoothly. I didn't use the ground fill that was on the guide and just wired everything normally.

### 2026-10-11 – I started trying to find all of the parts online. I ordered the ESP32 from Seeed Studio and the rest of the things from Amazon... and then my total was at $35 before I even included the PCB. I searche

**1.3h**

I started trying to find all of the parts online. I ordered the ESP32 from Seeed Studio and the rest of the things from Amazon... and then my total was at $35 before I even included the PCB. I searched for the cheapest things on Amazon, but it didn't go down much. Then, I realized that I could use AliExpress, and get everything for a dollar.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/4be66942faddeaf65eed715e7f523737bdd06ba316b1dc1868ba412710276bc3.png)

I hoped that nothing was a scam, though, because I really needed to save a lot of money using AliExpress. After changing the DHT11, the MPU-6050, and the keycaps, I reduced my total to 17.94, excluding the PCB

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/c56ddb771f6bd97e24e244d4433b058fe54e18470b499f28c5ccd81a818ed577.png)

I will probably reduce it a little more tomorrow, because the PCB is $12.47 counting shipping, which raises the total to just above $30.

### 2026-10-11 – I ordered the resistor from Digi-Key, but then the shipping raised my total above $33, which is the budget including the buffer. I had to order it from Amazon instead because AliExpress didn't specify

**1.2h**

I ordered the resistor from Digi-Key, but then the shipping raised my total above $33, which is the budget including the buffer. I had to order it from Amazon instead because AliExpress didn't specify the resistance for some reason.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/283f961405c8614f03812c0d23a464622dec6477d809b4611fb898733b8414b7.png)

My total was now 33 point something, so I had to go cheaper. I sadly had to remove the MX switches I got from Amazon and use AliExpress instead.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/ALyNJTAoKKQxkBhHkvpPIPXU2JTDxn4z/4a0f7d65c204bf531ff795975ce81e5935e80dc689217bf1b2d649c71d6ac23c.png)

I then put my PCB onto JLCPCB, and put all of my files onto Github.
